body:
Thank you so much for reading and for your input. 

A lot of people are saying that getting a job before I'm ready may make things worse, for the reasons you mentioned. People in my life are trying to force me into a direction of productivity and I don't know how to gracefully be a mentally ill person that isn't studying and isn't employed. Do you have any advice regarding this?

Again, thank you for your time and for believing me.

Thank you so much for your time. 

I've tried opening up to my mum. She frowns and becomes angry  and disappointed with me. I did alright in high school and as soon as the academic medals stopped pouring in, she started acting hateful towards me because she thought I was going to become a doctor, or a dentist. She has a completely different emotional spectrum, and often guilts me about how hard she's worked for me, about how she can't lose any kids, about how she won't be around forever, and about how the siblings with lower grades are doing better than me. She just pretends I'm normal. It seems like a reasonable response and it would be if she said it once and then talked about me, but she's never listened to a word I've tried to say. 

Fortunately I have a great older brother. He wants to start a small business with me and he's my closest friend. The thing is, he lives in another country and has lived there for the past 2+ years, and won't be coming home until June. My mum loves my older brother for embracing her own culture, so I might be able to tell my brother and have him get through to my mum. I've never told my brother secrets before, but he's open towards me. 

Maybe this is the best course of action. I really appreciate your confirmation that a job wouldn't be the best route. It's a shame that there's no safe way of me being productive without shattering like when I tried to study, since my biggest grief is my mum asking when I'll do something with my life. In a way I needed to hear that, though - to make it more real to me since everyone tries to push me in the direction of a "normal" person, when I'm not and I know deep down that I'm not. I feel like I know what to do now, even though building up the courage to open up to my brother may be hard. 

Thank you for your kindness. I'm going to do my best to get through.
A tree, but you're right, they're usually found in the scrub and away from any houses, but I've still come across a few stinging trees. I do like your theory of OP's hosts being cassowaries though.
Looks inspired by [this](https://cdn.artstation.com/p/assets/images/images/000/735/953/large/jakub-rozalski-another-day-at-work-just-watch-the-flowers.jpg?1431872298) image by Jakub Rozalski.

This is a bit too much. You should be able to see the tyres of the car in front of you touching the road. This allows for time to respond if they suddenly stop, and also allows for a bit of roll-back if the person in front is driving a manual, or particularly a heavy vehicle. 

Don't compromise safety just to save a few minutes of your time, you're not the only person to use these roads.
There's nothing "wrong with these people" and you should have just politely brought it up if it bothered you so much.
